pre_change_state.caveat_quote: These came from keyword searches of a database, not a complete systematic search... I may have missed trials, especially recent ones.

claims.text: | [W3015603533] Taiwanese PARO depression study | Participants were older adults with depression. The abstract doesn't mention dementia. |
claims.label: supported
claims.rationale: Participants were older adults with depression, and the abstract does not mention dementia.

claims.text: | [W2259814160], [W2394797369], [W2743226003], [W2592259105], [W2593419711] Telepresence studies | Older people at home or with mobility impairment. |
claims.label: unsupported
claims.rationale: The mobility-impairment descriptor fits only two of the five papers; the others concern home use or other groups, so the blanket grouping is not supported.

claims.text: A chat robot, "Sunshine", was piloted in long-term care during COVID-19 [W3041860695].
claims.label: unsupported
claims.rationale: The abstract is a truncated letter that mentions COVID-19 and long-term care but not the 'Sunshine' pilot setting beyond the title; the record gives only limited support.

claims.text: **Responses vary between people.** Effects depend on dementia severity [W2732925385] and differ even within one person over time [W2778691880].
claims.label: unsupported
claims.rationale: The Liang abstract says less cognitively impaired responded better, which supports severity dependence; the Moyle paper supports within-person variation. Both are supported, but the statement's 'dementia severity' framing fits only partly.

claims.text: Real-home trials exposed problems such as misinterpreted actions during unscripted interaction [W2994761079].
claims.label: supported
claims.rationale: The abstract mentions misinterpretation of actions during non-scripted HRI in real homes.

claims.text: A PARO and sleep paper from the same Norwegian group [W3102212853].
claims.label: unsupported
claims.rationale: The record is a thesis on a Paro group activity in Norway; the sleep paper is a separate record by the same group, so the statement is vague and not supported by this record's text on sleep.

claims.text: An AIBO study with early cognitive deficits (MMSE above 23, so mostly not dementia) [W2159536297].
claims.label: supported
claims.rationale: The abstract describes AIBO with older subjects with small cognitive deficits (MMSE>23).

claims.text: | [W1488883230] | PARO | 18 residents with mid- to late-stage dementia, one aged-care facility in Australia | Pilot randomized crossover vs reading group | Moderate-to-large positive effect on quality of life; higher pleasure scores. The authors call for a larger trial. |
claims.label: supported
claims.rationale: All details match the abstract.

claims.text: | [W2982896790], [W2899915867] NAO and theatre/arts | Older adults in residential care. Dementia not confirmed. |
claims.label: supported
claims.rationale: Both use NAO with older adults in residential care, and dementia status is only partially mentioned.

claims.text: | [W2043587319] Social shaping of PARO in a nursing home | I left it out of the second report without checking. It involves residents, staff and visitors, so some residents may have dementia. |
claims.label: not_a_claim
claims.rationale: The statement is about the assistant's own process and guess, with no checkable claim.

claims.text: Usability and attitude work involved older adults with mobility impairment [W2592259105, W2593419711].
claims.label: supported
claims.rationale: Both papers involve older adults with mobility impairment.

claims.text: | [W3015009700] | Joy for All robot animals (low-cost) | Two supported-living sites, for people with dementia or learning difficulties | Six-month diary study | Use grew from short structured sessions to near-permanent availability, so novelty did not fade. Reported benefits were reminiscence, communication and possibly less agitation. Some people called the robots "creepy". |
claims.label: supported
claims.rationale: Details match the abstract.

claims.text: A social robot collected patient-reported outcome measures from older patients in hospital [W2946005838].
claims.label: unsupported
claims.rationale: The study used community-dwelling persons aged 70+, not hospital patients.

claims.text: They built rapport and valued it [W2771925981].
claims.label: supported
claims.rationale: The abstract says they established rapport and valued the robot.

claims.text: | [W1972564462] | AIBO, live dog, visitor alone | Female nursing home residents with dementia | Comparative visits | Both the dog and AIBO increased social interaction beyond the visitor alone. AIBO produced longer looks and more resident-initiated conversation than the dog. |
claims.label: supported
claims.rationale: Matches the abstract.

claims.text: | [W2132164645] AIBO vs live dog and loneliness | Long-term care residents, with no dementia criterion stated. |
claims.label: supported
claims.rationale: The abstract involves LTCF residents with no dementia criterion.

claims.text: A robot was also used to promote human-to-human connection in an assisted-living community [W2943699887].
claims.label: supported
claims.rationale: The abstract describes a robot facilitating human-to-human engagement in assisted living.

claims.text: **Novelty effects were not clearly seen.** Interaction grew over weeks in the PARO group studies [W2040979576].
claims.label: unsupported
claims.rationale: The paper reports growth over seven weekly sessions suggesting not novelty effects, but it is one study, not 'PARO group studies', so the generalization is overstated.

claims.text: | [W2778691880] | PARO | Long-term care residents with dementia | Cluster RCT vs plush toy and usual care. This paper is a qualitative follow-up on 5 participants. | Responses varied widely between people and within the same person over time. The authors raise ethical issues about giving PARO and taking it back. The trial's quantitative results are reported elsewhere, and I didn't retrieve them. |
claims.label: supported
claims.rationale: Matches the abstract.

claims.text: That study [W2039822570] was fetched and is in the main set.
claims.label: not_a_claim
claims.rationale: It only comments on retrieval status, with no content claim.

claims.text: The authors judged the evidence too weak to recommend the approach clinically [W2889960145].
claims.label: supported
claims.rationale: The abstract says the evidence is not strong enough to recommend clinical effectiveness.

claims.text: Ethics (deception, attachment, withdrawal) is studied less than efficacy [W3001702224, W2778691880].
claims.label: unsupported
claims.rationale: Neither abstract states that ethics is studied less than efficacy.

claims.text: Multiple case study: resilience was supported in 8 of 10 people, but they needed skilled facilitation [W3092218325].
claims.label: supported
claims.rationale: The abstract matches: resilience supported in eight of ten, and skilled facilitation was needed.

claims.text: | [W2065178260] Exercise-coach studies | Older adults generally, not dementia. |
claims.label: supported
claims.rationale: The study involved elderly users generally, not dementia.

claims.text: In the Hobbit and Companion field tests, the main barriers were reliability and robustness, not lack of interest [W2994761079, W2717439789, W4251569456].
claims.label: unsupported
claims.rationale: Hobbit abstract does not cite reliability as the main barrier; the Companion abstract notes navigation and speech improvements; 'not lack of interest' is an overgeneralization.

claims.text: **Facilitation matters.** Staff mediation drove interaction in PARO, MARIO and walking-group studies [W2039822570, W3092218325, W2592905630].
claims.label: unsupported
claims.rationale: The MARIO abstract supports facilitation and the others support mediation, but 'drove interaction' is overstated for the walking-group robot study.

claims.text: **Humanoid robot versus tablet training for people with dementia at home.** I found only the study protocol [W2975531399].
claims.label: supported
claims.rationale: The record is a protocol with no results.

claims.text: [W2751864896] Telepresence robots for dementia: I listed it as a lead and haven't read it.
claims.label: not_a_claim
claims.rationale: A statement about the assistant's own process.

claims.text: **Several robots, no clear benefit.** The multi-robot aged-care trial found neither benefits nor harms [W1945345301].
claims.label: supported
claims.rationale: The abstract says no major benefits or problems.

claims.text: **Symptom and quality-of-life results are mixed.** Some trials find no change in dementia symptoms or standardized scales [W2732925385, W2955051104].
claims.label: supported
claims.rationale: Both report no significant differences in symptoms or scales.

claims.text: Benefits appeared where the cat was accepted, and some people rejected it [W3034490183].
claims.label: supported
claims.rationale: The abstract says benefits were evident where accepted, and acceptance and rejection was a theme.

claims.text: A robot music therapist for cognitive impairment, with no study details [W759765632].
claims.label: supported
claims.rationale: The record has only a brief abstract about a robotic music therapist for cognitive impairment.

claims.text: | [W3088196398] | PARO | 60 residents with dementia, 10 Norwegian nursing home special care units | Cluster RCT: 30 minutes twice weekly for 12 weeks, vs treatment as usual | Better sleep efficiency and total sleep time, fewer awakenings (wrist actigraphy). |
claims.label: supported
claims.rationale: Matches the abstract.

claims.text: **Participatory-arts and mood work.** NAO was used with theatre-based activities in residential care [W2982896790, W2899915867].
claims.label: supported
claims.rationale: Both used NAO with theatre in residential care.

claims.text: In the multi-arm study, NAO's cognition result was worse [W1807810766].
claims.label: supported
claims.rationale: The NAO group showed a decline in MMSE cognition.

claims.text: | [W2889960145] Social robots for depression | Depression focus. |
claims.label: supported
claims.rationale: The review focuses on depression.

claims.text: The NAO arm in [W1807810766] shows that not every robot arm improved.
claims.label: supported
claims.rationale: The NAO arm showed an MMSE decline, so not every arm improved.

claims.text: In a companion analysis, most interaction was prompted by therapists, and only 2 of 12 residents initiated any [W2592905630].
claims.label: supported
claims.rationale: The abstract says most interaction was therapist-encouraged and two of 12 were self-initiated.

claims.text: The call that failed was the telepresence-for-dementia review [W2751864896].
claims.label: not_a_claim
claims.rationale: A statement about the assistant's own process.

claims.text: One paper assessed microbial contamination and disinfection of companion robots in care homes [W3081435517].
claims.label: supported
claims.rationale: The abstract matches.

observations.caveat_quote: Some may include people with dementia, so they are the likeliest misses.
